subject: Hosted API pricing — Mediflow monthly burn + 99th TPS plan
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@mediflow.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan@mediflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick recap + a couple clarifying asks (hosted API pricing)

Thanks again for the 30-min call this morning — really appreciate the clear context on where Mediflow is headed. I promised a short recap and two items we need to lock down to put together a firm hosted API proposal and an optional pilot SOW. High-level summary below.

What we heard (quick):
- Primary use case: clinical document summarization and authorization routing. Most traffic comes from batch ingestion (end-of-day) plus spikes during morning sync window.
- Latency SLO: 99th <= 450ms for short summaries (avg tokens per request ~550).
- Desired start: pilot in APAC region (GCP singapore) with potential dedicated capacity later.

Two clarifying asks (to finalize cost modeling):
1) A realistic expected monthly token volume range for months 1–3 (min, expected, max). If you can give rough daily profiles that helps (eg. 200k/day with 6x peak on Mondays).
2) Peak TPS (99th percentile) we should plan capacity for during the morning sync window — is 30 TPS conservative, or can you see higher short peaks (60–80 TPS for a few minutes)?

Attachments: I attached a one-page traffic template and a draft SOW we can iterate on. Please mark any numbers as estimates and we'll convert to pricing bands.

Next steps: if you can reply with the two items above by end of week I’ll run unit econ scenarios and return 2 proposal options — (A) hosted pay-as-you-go with burst tolerances, (B) 3-month pilot reserved slab + guaranteed SLA.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@mediflow.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan@mediflow.ai>
Date: 2025-12-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple clarifying asks (hosted API pricing)

Thanks Vivek — good recap and clear asks. Answers below (numbers are provisional; will confirm with infra team tomorrow):

1) Monthly token range (months 1–3):
- Min: 10M tokens / month (pilot-limited usage)
- Expected: 45M tokens / month (onboarding + increasing ingestion)
- Max: 120M tokens / month (full ingestion + some synthetic traffic for QA)

Daily profile: baseline ~1.5M tokens/day, spike days up to 9M tokens (roughly 6x baseline) — spikes concentrated Mon/Tue mornings during batch processing.

2) Peak TPS (99th): our infra team says current backend can emit ~55 TPS during the morning window for short summaries; with retries and client-side bursts we want to plan for up to 80 TPS for short windows (2–5 minutes).

Couple of extra notes:
- Average request size ~550 tokens in & 40 tokens out (so token accounting is roughly in-dominant).
- For the pilot, we’d like to test both standard model and a quantized variant if you support that — cost tradeoffs are important.

We’ll review your SOW and the traffic template; attaching a quick internal note (will share the infra confirmation tomorrow).

Best,
Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Head of Product, Mediflow
alyssa@mediflow.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Turner <alyssa@mediflow.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-12-03T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple clarifying asks (hosted API pricing)

Thanks for the numbers Alyssa — super helpful. I did a quick back-of-envelope on unit-econ and a couple of clarifying items that will materially change the hosted pricing bands:

Prelim unit-econ assumptions (please confirm):
- Avg request token footprint: 550 in + 40 out = 590 tokens total (we price on tokens generated + prompt).
- Expected monthly volume (we’ll model all three): 10M / 45M / 120M tokens.
- 99th TPS to provision for short bursts: plan for 80 TPS peak.

Prelim pricing bands (hosted, per 1M tokens) — ranges reflect batch vs worst-case burst handling and caching options:
- Pilot (no reserved capacity, pay-as-you-go + auto-burst): $85–$120 per 1M tokens (higher tail due to burst premium and no reserved pool).
- 3-month reserved pilot slab (commit & discounted egress/burst): $55–$75 per 1M tokens depending on exact SLA and burst allowance.

Key knobs that change the math:
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (can reduce billed tokens significantly if you have a lot of shared context).
- Quantized model variants: ~20–35% cheaper per token at potential quality delta (we can run a quick eval on your samples).
- Burst duration: if bursts are always <3 minutes and rare, we can route to a higher-cost burst pool only during those windows to keep regular rates lower.

Requests:
- Can Mediflow share a short sample set (5–10 typical documents) we can run on both model variants to produce a quick quality vs cost delta?
- Also would like the traffic CSV exported from the template (per-minute granularity for 7 days) to size batching and KV cache benefit.

If you’re comfortable, we’ll produce two short proposal options by Friday: 1) Pay-as-you-go hosted with burst caps and expected $/1M estimate; 2) 3-month reserved pilot slab with explicit SLA and unit price bands. We’ll call out the conditions where we switch to reserved or add dedicated capacity.

Karthik
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-12-04T14:32:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps + pilot proposal timeline (Mediflow)

Perfect — thanks Alyssa and Karthik. Quick next steps and timeline:

1) Alyssa/Ethan: please share the 7-day per-minute traffic extract and 5 example documents by EOD Thursday (2025-12-11) so we can run the quality/cost probes.
2) Karthik/Monica: we’ll model three scenarios (10M / 45M / 120M tokens) and produce two proposal docs (PAYG vs 3-month reserved pilot) + a short ROI table showing $/1M tokens and expected monthly bill. Aim to have these back by Friday 2025-12-12.
3) DocuSign/SOW: I’ll drop a DocuSign link for the pilot SOW (SOW v0.3 attached) once we align on the pilot slab. If Mediflow wants faster start we can do a 30-day rolling pilot with a lighter commit.

I’ll include an explicit line item for APAC region routing and a burst buffer allowance configured for up to 80 TPS for 5 minutes in the pilot plan.

Thanks — Vivek
